currentContext.business: Carraro India Limited, a subsidiary of the Italy-based Carraro Group, designs, manufactures and supplies axles, transmission systems, gears and related driveline components for off-highway vehicles - agricultural tractors and construction vehicles such as backhoe loaders, telescopic boom handlers, soil compactors, cranes, self-loading concrete mixers and small motor graders. Its customers are OEMs, primarily India-based (including international OEMs with Indian operations), with exports routed largely through holding company Carraro SpA; the Company describes itself as a technology-driven integrated supplier whose products are critical components of its customers' final products. Alongside manufacturing it sells engineering services to external customers, drawing on its Ranjangaon R&D centre and its R&D subsidiary Carraro Technologies India Private Limited, and supplies spare parts and aftermarket support.

currentContext.strengths: Designated global centre of excellence for agricultural transmissions within the Carraro Group and one of the Group's largest manufacturing locations, positioning it for future product programmes, technology transfers and global sourcing|Long-lived OEM relationships: the top 10 customers by revenue contribution have engaged the Company continuously for at least 15 years, and six new customers were onboarded during the year|Products are critical components of customers' final products, giving high embeddedness in OEM platforms|Strong position in the domestic non-captive 4WD axle market, deepened during the year in higher-value transmission applications|Engineering depth: in-house R&D centre plus R&D subsidiary Carraro Technologies India Private Limited, connected to Group engineering hubs in Italy, China and Luxembourg; engineering services revenue reached about `100 Million in 2025-26|Vertically integrated manufacturing at one site - cast machining, heat treatment, gear manufacturing, assembly, painting, prototyping and testing across an 84,000 sq. m. driveline plant and a 78,000 sq. m. gear plant|Deepening localisation of raw materials and components, supporting supply-chain resilience and cost optimisation|Early positioning in off-highway electrification through the Montra Electric e-transmission engineering services agreement and CVT / higher-horsepower platform development
currentContext.strategies: Five strategic priorities anchored in resilience, trust and future readiness - reading industry direction early, deepening customer partnerships and investing in next-generation technologies across the agricultural and construction equipment markets.|Ride the structural shift to 4WD and higher-horsepower tractors, where advanced axle and transmission demand sits squarely in the Company's core strengths.|Deepen localisation of raw materials and components, progressing towards a medium-term localisation target of 86-88% (78.1% in 2025-26, up from 77.0%), to improve supply security, shorten lead times and strengthen cost competitiveness.|Operate a dual-sourcing strategy with a minimum of two suppliers per component across a 247-supplier base (177 domestic), build long-term supplier partnerships through capability-building programmes and technical workshops, and selectively integrate critical components vertically.|Defend the driveline moat through deep application expertise, integrated OEM co-engineering and high switching costs backed by long validation cycles and deeply embedded product architecture.|Build future-ready platforms for electrification: develop electric and hydrostatic-electric drivelines, pursue joint technology development with the Carraro Group across electric, hybrid and advanced transmission platforms, provide engineering services for e-transmission industrialisation, develop CVT technology for future tractor applications and invest continually in EV transmission design, validation and specialised engineering skills.|Scale engineering services into a standalone growth engine - about `100 Million generated during 2025-26, with a new agreement with Montra Electric to industrialise and supply e-transmissions.|Invest ahead of demand in manufacturing capacity: `417 Million deployed in 2025-26 across telescopic handler axle programmes, advanced transmission platforms and additional capacity, with the Board approving a programme to further increase annual axle production capacity from 2026-27.|Broaden customer reach and supply-chain strength - first authorised service centre opened at Faridabad, plus deeper localisation and supplier development.|Sustain innovation throughput from the in-house R&D centre and the Group's global engineering network (Italy, China, Luxembourg): 16 prototypes developed during the year and four taken into production, focused on higher-horsepower drivelines and advanced transmission technologies.|Continue evolving from a manufacturing-focused organisation into an integrated engineering and technology-driven enterprise, strengthened by the integration of Carraro Technologies India Private Limited and its Pune engineering centre.
currentContext.expansion: Carraro India is expanding ahead of demand at its Ranjangaon, Pune site. To support expected demand growth across both agricultural and construction equipment applications, the Board approved a capital expenditure programme of approximately `623 Million to expand axle manufacturing capacity from about 134,028 units to about 154,160 units over the next 18 months. During 2025-26 the Company incurred capital expenditure of approximately `417 Million on telescopic handler (TBH) axle production, a new high-performance transmission range for agricultural applications, and incremental capacity for 2025-26 sales; the Board's newly approved programme is a further, separate step and the Chairman's message describes a new phase of investments and capacity expansion starting in 2026-27. At the driveline plant (Plant 1) the expansion is phased: Phase 1 covers a paint shop and finished-goods warehouse, Phase 2 a new assembly line and incoming-material warehouse, and Phase 3 a new administrative building, alongside the additional approved axle capacity. Manufacturing upgrades during the year included sealed-quench furnaces and a Mazak machining centre. Other capability additions in the period were the inauguration of the Company's first authorised service centre at Faridabad and continued investment in localisation, automation and process improvement; the pipeline the capacity is being built for is the 4WD axle ramp, the TBH axle programme for an international OEM, higher-horsepower transmission programmes and a bull-gear nomination starting 2027-28.
currentContext.mdna: Structural 2WD-to-4WD tractor shift: in 2025-26, 23%-25% of the tractor market above 40 HP shifted from 2WD to 4WD, with 4WD tractor volumes expected to grow at a CAGR of 19.1%, well ahead of conventional tractor segments.|India contributes nearly 35-40% of global tractor demand, and growing preference for higher-horsepower tractors is increasing demand for advanced transmission systems and axle solutions.|Adoption of TREM IV/V norms is expected to support premiumisation and export opportunities.|Domestic tractor industry recorded its best-ever annual volumes in 2025-26 with wholesale sales crossing the 10 Lakh unit milestone; total tractor sales including exports reached approximately 12.6 Lakh units and production exceeded 11.5 Lakh units.|Long-term tractor outlook remains favourable on rising mechanisation, government support (SMAM, Custom Hiring Centres), higher rural incomes, improved credit access through the KCC ecosystem and rising labour costs pushing mechanisation.|Construction equipment is a two-sided story: domestic sales fell approximately 2% year-on-year to 136,995 units on slower project execution and delayed awards (ICEMA data cited in the Board's Report shows a ~7% decline to 1,13,229 units), while exports rose nearly 32% on demand from African, Middle Eastern and Latin American markets.|Infrastructure-led demand anchors the medium term: PM GatiShakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline (over USD 1.4 Trillion), Bharatmala, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, PMGSY and a `2.93 Lakh Crore railway capital outlay in the Union Budget 2026-27.|Export competitiveness and deepening localisation (more than 95% of construction equipment sold domestically is now made in India) are the supply-side gains expected to carry India towards being the second-largest construction equipment market by 2030.|Margin levers stated by management: operating leverage on higher volumes, disciplined cost management, continued localisation gains and a richer product mix with greater contribution from high-value 4WD axles and TBH programmes.|Mix shift towards exports: export sales contributed 36% of total revenue, up from 32.8% in the prior year, led by TBH axles for a global OEM and recovering demand for tractor axles in international markets.|Market position underpinning the demand narrative: 60%+ share of non-captive 4WD tractor axles (>40 HP), 100% of non-captive AG tractor transmissions (>40 HP) and 60%+ of non-captive construction vehicle transmissions.|Off-highway industry structural shifts - tightening emission norms, fuel-efficiency and technology preferences, and the early-stage emergence of electrification in agricultural tractors - are pushing OEMs to invest in engineering and electrification roadmaps, widening the Company's engineering services opportunity.

risks.note: A large part of revenue comes from a few OEM customers; if any cuts orders, shifts to in-house production or moves to a competitor, volumes and plant utilisation are significantly affected. Mitigated by widening the customer base, an updated product portfolio and long-term supply agreements (LTAs).

Reliance on Carraro Group entities for technology and procurement could limit operational independence. Mitigated by building design and testing capability in India, developing local suppliers for critical parts and formal agreements with the Group on technology support and supply continuity.

A high volume of intercompany transactions with Group entities may raise governance and compliance concerns; managed through Audit Committee review, periodic transfer-pricing benchmarking and disclosure aligned with the Companies Act and SEBI LODR.

risks.risk: Seasonality and cyclicality of end markets
risks.note: Demand is linked to the farming season and to construction and commercial vehicle cycles, causing revenue and plant workload to swing sharply quarter to quarter; balanced through segment mix and flexible manpower arrangements.

The pace of OEM investment in electrification and hybridisation is uncertain, and continued reliance on conventional mechanical drivelines risks share loss if customers transition faster than the Company's e-axle and hybrid offering matures; mitigated by co-developing e-axle and hybrid platforms with Group R&D and phasing capex to confirmed programme awards.

risks.risk: Raw material cost volatility and margin pressure
risks.note: Steel, alloy and other input costs remain volatile while OEM price negotiations lag cost movements, compressing realised margins; addressed through indexed pricing clauses where feasible, efficiency and cost-reduction projects.

Shipping-route disruption, tariff actions and concentrated sourcing for certain components expose input costs and delivery schedules to events outside the Company's control; mitigated by dual-sourcing of critical items, strategic buffer stock and scenario-based monitoring of freight and landed costs.

Increasing use of technology raises exposure to cyber-attacks, while DPDPA obligations add compliance burden around personal data handling; addressed through an updated IT security framework implemented across group entities and third-party consultant support for DPDPA compliance.

risks.risk: Internal market overlap with related entities
risks.note: Competitive dynamics within the broader industry and potential overlaps with related Carraro entities may impact market positioning; managed through geographical segmentation, market-specific strategies and enhancing business independence via purchase of intellectual property rights.

Heat treatment of gears and shafts is the most energy-intensive stage of driveline manufacturing, so energy costs are a significant portion of operating expenditure, and dependence on non-renewable fuels such as PNG and diesel exposes the Company to energy price volatility, carbon-related regulation and customer emissions scrutiny (BRSR material issues table).

one-line thesis: Carraro India delivered a beat-and-raise FY26 with 25% revenue growth and 60bps margin expansion to 10.8%, driven by the structural GST-induced shift to 4WD tractors and robust construction exports. While FY27 guidance is cautiously tempered to 4-8% due to geopolitical volatility, the medium-term trajectory remains intact with a raised FY30 revenue target of INR 3,500-4,000 crores and deepening localization (78% to ~88%) supporting profitability.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,255 Cr (+25% YoY); Q4 Revenue: INR 606 Cr (+37% YoY). EBITDA: INR 247.5 Cr (+33% YoY), Margin 10.8% (+60bps YoY); Q4 EBITDA Margin 11.6%. PAT: INR 130.6 Cr (+48% YoY); Normalized PAT excludes INR 8.4 Cr one-off provision reversal in other income. Order Book: Robust visibility in TBH exports; Domestic BHL sales +9% despite market -10%. Net Debt: D/E improved to 0.27x (from 0.42x); Working Capital days reduced to 38 from 45.
guidance: Revenue Growth FY27: Cautious 4-8% (base case 8-12% pending macro stability); Margin: Upward trajectory from 10.8% (no specific bps guidance due to volatility); Order Inflow: Strong TBH export pipeline; Capex FY27: ~INR 130 Cr focused on telescopic handler axles and high-HP transmissions.
order book & pipeline: Tele Boom Handler (TBH) program ramping for major international OEM with visibility for next 6 months; Targeting INR 30 Cr annual revenue from TBH by FY29; Domestic BHL driveline sales grew 9% vs market decline of 10%; New bull gear nomination secured (INR 15 Cr/year starting FY28).
segment / subsidiary detail: Agri Vehicles: INR 1,019 Cr (+19% YoY), driven by 4WD axle transition (market share est. 24% of >40HP segment); Construction Vehicles: INR 984 Cr (+31% YoY), led by exports (+37%); Gears: Subdued but pipeline strengthening; Engineering Services: INR 10 Cr revenue, highlighted by INR 17.5 Cr contract with Montra Electric for EV transmissions.
growth verticals / optionality: 4WD penetration rising from ~24% to projected 40-45% over 3-5 years; High-HP transmission SOP Turkey (FY27) and India (FY28); EV transmission industrialization with Montra Electric; Aftermarket network expansion; Localization target of 86-88% by FY28/29.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 Margin 10.8% driven by operating leverage, product mix (4WD), and localization (78% RM localized). Q4 RM % increase attributed to adverse product mix (rush dispatches) rather than commodity inflation. Pass-through mechanism typically lags 3 months. Labor availability cited as emerging cost pressure.
capex / expansion: FY26 Actual: INR 41.7 Cr (Telescopic handler axles, high-HP transmission programs, capacity expansion). FY27 Guidance: ~INR 130 Cr.
capital allocation: Dividend: INR 6.75/share (Final), ~30% payout ratio. Balance sheet strengthening prioritized (D/E 0.27x). Reinvestment in capacity and technology for FY30 growth targets.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting energy prices/supply chain (H1 FY27 risk); Monsoon uncertainty affecting rural demand; Global tariff volatility (US/Europe); Labor availability constraints; Raw material price fluctuations.
management quality / tone: Confident on structural long-term trends (4WD shift, export hub status) but prudently cautious on near-term FY27 guidance due to macro/geopolitical volatility; Emphasized execution discipline and 'watchtower' monitoring of costs.
non-obvious takeaways: Management explicitly linked the 4WD surge to GST reduction narrowing the price gap with 2WD, creating a permanent structural shift rather than cyclical bump; Q4 margin dip in specific axle categories was a strategic choice to prioritize customer supply continuity over immediate cost efficiency, absorbing fixed costs better overall.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.

hero.oneLiner: Carraro India is an independent Tier-1 supplier of axles, transmission systems and gears for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs, and the Carraro Group's designated global centre of excellence for agricultural transmissions.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Carraro India is an independent Tier-1 supplier of axles, transmission systems and gears for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs, and the Carraro Group's designated global centre of excellence for agricultural transmissions.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Carraro India Limited, a subsidiary of the Italy-based Carraro Group, designs, manufactures and supplies axles, transmission systems, gears and related driveline components for off-highway vehicles - agricultural tractors and construction vehicles such as backhoe loaders, telescopic boom handlers, soil compactors, cranes, self-loading concrete mixers and small motor graders. Its customers are OEMs, primarily India-based (including international OEMs with Indian operations), with exports routed largely through holding company Carraro SpA; the Company describes itself as a technology-driven integrated supplier whose products are critical components of its customers' final products. Alongside manufacturing it sells engineering services to external customers, drawing on its Ranjangaon R&D centre and its R&D subsidiary Carraro Technologies India Private Limited, and supplies spare parts and aftermarket support.

segment_detail.body: Agri Vehicles: INR 1,019 Cr (+19% YoY), driven by 4WD axle transition (market share est. 24% of >40HP segment); Construction Vehicles: INR 984 Cr (+31% YoY), led by exports (+37%); Gears: Subdued but pipeline strengthening; Engineering Services: INR 10 Cr revenue, highlighted by INR 17.5 Cr contract with Montra Electric for EV transmissions.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Transmission Systems:** 35-50 HP Tractor Transmissions (T40 and T50), 50-90 HP Tractor Transmissions, Up to 150 HP Tractor Transmissions, Hydrostatic Transmissions for Construction Equipment, T100 EVO-HD, T100 CVT, T135 tractor transmission, TCB80 Series, TCB80 SPS Series
- **Axles:** 4WD Portal Axles (30-50 HP), 4WD Planetary Axles (49-135 HP), Steering Axles ACP (1.9 5T UVW), Steering Axles Trunnion (1.9-5T UVW), Rigid Hypoid Axles (5-17T UVW), Telescopic boom handler (TBH) axles, Backhoe loader (BHL) driveline systems
- **Gears:** Precision gears and gear shafts for captive consumption and third-party customers, Ring gears and shafts for industrial and automotive vehicles, Bull gears (nominated by a major OEM from 2027-28)
- **Engineering Services:** Application engineering, virtual validation, prototyping, laboratory and field testing, E-transmission industrialisation and supply for electric agricultural tractors (Montra Electric agreement)
- **Aftermarket Solutions:** OEM-original spare parts and lifecycle support through the authorised service network

end_markets.body:

- Construction equipment - backhoe loaders, telescopic boom handlers, soil compactors, self-loading concrete mixers, compact wheel loaders, small motor graders
- Harvesters, forklifts and material-handling equipment
- Industrial and automotive vehicles (gears, shafts and ring gears)
- India - operations and customers across 07 states and 02 union territories
- Exports to 14 countries, contributing 35.11% of total turnover (BRSR); routed largely via holding company Carraro SpA

certifications.body:

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Tele Boom Handler (TBH) program ramping for major international OEM with visibility for next 6 months; Targeting INR 30 Cr annual revenue from TBH by FY29; Domestic BHL driveline sales grew 9% vs market decline of 10%; New bull gear nomination secured (INR 15 Cr/year starting FY28).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth FY27: Cautious 4-8% (base case 8-12% pending macro stability); Margin: Upward trajectory from 10.8% (no specific bps guidance due to volatility); Order Inflow: Strong TBH export pipeline; Capex FY27: ~INR 130 Cr focused on telescopic handler axles and high-HP transmissions.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: 4WD penetration rising from ~24% to projected 40-45% over 3-5 years; High-HP transmission SOP Turkey (FY27) and India (FY28); EV transmission industrialization with Montra Electric; Aftermarket network expansion; Localization target of 86-88% by FY28/29.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural 2WD-to-4WD tractor shift: in 2025-26, 23%-25% of the tractor market above 40 HP shifted from 2WD to 4WD, with 4WD tractor volumes expected to grow at a CAGR of 19.1%, well ahead of conventional tractor segments.
- India contributes nearly 35-40% of global tractor demand, and growing preference for higher-horsepower tractors is increasing demand for advanced transmission systems and axle solutions.
- Adoption of TREM IV/V norms is expected to support premiumisation and export opportunities.
- Domestic tractor industry recorded its best-ever annual volumes in 2025-26 with wholesale sales crossing the 10 Lakh unit milestone; total tractor sales including exports reached approximately 12.6 Lakh units and production exceeded 11.5 Lakh units.
- Long-term tractor outlook remains favourable on rising mechanisation, government support (SMAM, Custom Hiring Centres), higher rural incomes, improved credit access through the KCC ecosystem and rising labour costs pushing mechanisation.
- Construction equipment is a two-sided story: domestic sales fell approximately 2% year-on-year to 136,995 units on slower project execution and delayed awards (ICEMA data cited in the Board's Report shows a ~7% decline to 1,13,229 units), while exports rose nearly 32% on demand from African, Middle Eastern and Latin American markets.
- Infrastructure-led demand anchors the medium term: PM GatiShakti, the National Infrastructure Pipeline (over USD 1.4 Trillion), Bharatmala, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission, AMRUT 2.0, PMGSY and a `2.93 Lakh Crore railway capital outlay in the Union Budget 2026-27.
- Export competitiveness and deepening localisation (more than 95% of construction equipment sold domestically is now made in India) are the supply-side gains expected to carry India towards being the second-largest construction equipment market by 2030.
- Margin levers stated by management: operating leverage on higher volumes, disciplined cost management, continued localisation gains and a richer product mix with greater contribution from high-value 4WD axles and TBH programmes.
- Mix shift towards exports: export sales contributed 36% of total revenue, up from 32.8% in the prior year, led by TBH axles for a global OEM and recovering demand for tractor axles in international markets.
- Market position underpinning the demand narrative: 60%+ share of non-captive 4WD tractor axles (>40 HP), 100% of non-captive AG tractor transmissions (>40 HP) and 60%+ of non-captive construction vehicle transmissions.
- Off-highway industry structural shifts - tightening emission norms, fuel-efficiency and technology preferences, and the early-stage emergence of electrification in agricultural tractors - are pushing OEMs to invest in engineering and electrification roadmaps, widening the Company's engineering services opportunity.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 Margin 10.8% driven by operating leverage, product mix (4WD), and localization (78% RM localized). Q4 RM % increase attributed to adverse product mix (rush dispatches) rather than commodity inflation. Pass-through mechanism typically lags 3 months. Labor availability cited as emerging cost pressure.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend: INR 6.75/share (Final), ~30% payout ratio. Balance sheet strengthening prioritized (D/E 0.27x). Reinvestment in capacity and technology for FY30 growth targets.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Carraro India is expanding ahead of demand at its Ranjangaon, Pune site. To support expected demand growth across both agricultural and construction equipment applications, the Board approved a capital expenditure programme of approximately `623 Million to expand axle manufacturing capacity from about 134,028 units to about 154,160 units over the next 18 months. During 2025-26 the Company incurred capital expenditure of approximately `417 Million on telescopic handler (TBH) axle production, a new high-performance transmission range for agricultural applications, and incremental capacity for 2025-26 sales; the Board's newly approved programme is a further, separate step and the Chairman's message describes a new phase of investments and capacity expansion starting in 2026-27. At the driveline plant (Plant 1) the expansion is phased: Phase 1 covers a paint shop and finished-goods warehouse, Phase 2 a new assembly line and incoming-material warehouse, and Phase 3 a new administrative building, alongside the additional approved axle capacity. Manufacturing upgrades during the year included sealed-quench furnaces and a Mazak machining centre. Other capability additions in the period were the inauguration of the Company's first authorised service centre at Faridabad and continued investment in localisation, automation and process improvement; the pipeline the capacity is being built for is the 4WD axle ramp, the TBH axle programme for an international OEM, higher-horsepower transmission programmes and a bull-gear nomination starting 2027-28.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on structural long-term trends (4WD shift, export hub status) but prudently cautious on near-term FY27 guidance due to macro/geopolitical volatility; Emphasized execution discipline and 'watchtower' monitoring of costs.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Designated global centre of excellence for agricultural transmissions within the Carraro Group and one of the Group's largest manufacturing locations, positioning it for future product programmes, technology transfers and global sourcing
- Long-lived OEM relationships: the top 10 customers by revenue contribution have engaged the Company continuously for at least 15 years, and six new customers were onboarded during the year
- Products are critical components of customers' final products, giving high embeddedness in OEM platforms
- Strong position in the domestic non-captive 4WD axle market, deepened during the year in higher-value transmission applications
- Engineering depth: in-house R&D centre plus R&D subsidiary Carraro Technologies India Private Limited, connected to Group engineering hubs in Italy, China and Luxembourg; engineering services revenue reached about `100 Million in 2025-26
- Vertically integrated manufacturing at one site - cast machining, heat treatment, gear manufacturing, assembly, painting, prototyping and testing across an 84,000 sq. m. driveline plant and a 78,000 sq. m. gear plant
- Deepening localisation of raw materials and components, supporting supply-chain resilience and cost optimisation
- Early positioning in off-highway electrification through the Montra Electric e-transmission engineering services agreement and CVT / higher-horsepower platform development

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting energy prices/supply chain (H1 FY27 risk); Monsoon uncertainty affecting rural demand; Global tariff volatility (US/Europe); Labor availability constraints; Raw material price fluctuations.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Management explicitly linked the 4WD surge to GST reduction narrowing the price gap with 2WD, creating a permanent structural shift rather than cyclical bump; Q4 margin dip in specific axle categories was a strategic choice to prioritize customer supply continuity over immediate cost efficiency, absorbing fixed costs better overall.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Five strategic priorities anchored in resilience, trust and future readiness - reading industry direction early, deepening customer partnerships and investing in next-generation technologies across the agricultural and construction equipment markets.
- Ride the structural shift to 4WD and higher-horsepower tractors, where advanced axle and transmission demand sits squarely in the Company's core strengths.
- Deepen localisation of raw materials and components, progressing towards a medium-term localisation target of 86-88% (78.1% in 2025-26, up from 77.0%), to improve supply security, shorten lead …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rural cash flow sensitivity and monsoon dependence | TAFE Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Carraro's 4WD axle growth mirrors industry-wide shift benefiting large OEMs like TAFE who are pivoting to 4WD platforms. |
| Export market volatility and tariff risks | Escorts Kubota | beneficiary | Med | Shared exposure to export-led construction equipment demand and domestic 4WD transition trends. |
| Supply chain localization pressures | Unorganized Gear/Axis Vendors | loser | High | Carraro's push to 88% localization and in-house engineering services may squeeze smaller, less technologically advanced tier-2 vendors. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Listing] Carraro India Limited was listed in December 2024 on NSE and BSE; the deck's journey slide records the 2023 reorganisation of IPR and R&D under which IPR for all products sold in the domestic market was transferred to CIL.
- [Labour code] FY26 included an exceptional item of INR -95 million described as the "Impact of New Labor Code of INR 95 Million".
- [Customs] Other income included a one-time provision written-back of INR 88.07 million pertaining to customs related proceedings on account of a reassessment performed by the Company for the period.
- [Industry outlook] Markets and Markets data in the deck shows the 4WD Indian tractor market growing from 80k units (2019A) to 213k (2024E) to 600k (2029E) at a +23.0% CAGR, versus the 2WD market at +2.8% CAGR, and the total Indian construction vehicle market at +5.0% CAGR.
- [Recognition] Customer awards cited include Mahindra Group (Supplier Excellence - Spare Parts Service; Superior Performance for FY25 & FY26), Caterpillar (Supplier Excellence Recognition 2024), Escorts Kubota, Swaraj Tractors, Bull Machines and Manitou Equipment.
